practiceQuestions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made elementary education a fundamental right under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children between the ages of 6 and 14 a fundamental right. It was operationalized via the RTE Act, 2009 in April 2010.

practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) is early childhood care and education (ECCE) for children below six years provided?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 45 of the Constitution was amended by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 to direct the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of the Samagra Shiksha Scheme?
opts: Providing higher education loans to university students
Subsuming SSA, RMSA, and Teacher Education into a single school education scheme from pre-school to class XII
Promoting technical and vocational training exclusively for rural women
Financing foreign universities operating within Indian territory
practiceQuestions.sol: Samagra Shiksha is an integrated scheme for school education spanning from pre-school to senior secondary level (Class XII). It subsumed Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), and Teacher Education (TE).

practiceQuestions.q: When was the Mid-Day Meal Scheme (now known as PM POSHAN Scheme) officially launched as a centrally sponsored scheme?
practiceQuestions.sol: The National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (Mid-Day Meal Scheme) was launched on August 15, 1995, as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme to enhance enrollment, retention, and attendance while improving nutritional levels.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies is the apex advisory body on education to the Central and State Governments, responsible for implementing the National Education Policy?
opts: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration (NIEPA)
practiceQuestions.sol: CABE is the oldest and the most important advisory body of the Government of India in the field of education, playing a leading role in evolving a national policy on education.

practiceQuestions.q: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 mandates private unaided schools to reserve what percentage of entry-level seats for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups?
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, 2009 mandates private unaided schools to reserve at least 25% of their entry-level seats for children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups, providing free elementary education.

practiceQuestions.q: Which flagship higher education scheme was launched in 2013 to improve the quality of state higher educational institutions and promote research and innovation?
practiceQuestions.sol: Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at providing strategic funding to eligible state higher educational institutions to attain higher levels of equity, access, and excellence.

practiceQuestions.q: Education was transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule by which Constitutional Amendment?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 transferred five subjects, including education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice, from the State List to the Concurrent List.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary target group under the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' scheme regarding education?
opts: Adult illiterate women above 35 years of age
Girl children to prevent gender-biased sex selective elimination and ensure their survival, protection, and education
Post-graduate girl students pursuing STEM courses
Orphan girls residing in urban municipal shelter homes
practiceQuestions.sol: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) is a tri-ministerial initiative addressing the declining Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues of empowerment of women and girls, focusing heavily on preventing dropouts and promoting girl child education.

practiceQuestions.q: Which initiative was launched by the Ministry of Education to ensure that every child in India attains foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) by Grade 3 by the year 2026-27?
practiceQuestions.sol: National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN Bharat) was launched under Samagra Shiksha to create an enabling environment to ensure universal acquisition of foundational literacy and numeracy by grade 3 by 2026-27.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the structural devolution under the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts impact the governance of educational welfare schemes at the grassroots level?
opts: It centralizes administrative control entirely with the Union Ministry of Education, bypassing state machinery.
It transfers functional jurisdiction over primary and secondary schools to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) for local monitoring and implementation.
It abolishes all state-level school boards and empowers village panchayats to grant university degrees.
It shifts all educational expenditures onto private corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds without state oversight.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 11th and 12th Schedules added by the 73rd and 74th Amendments explicitly include 'education, including primary and secondary schools' as matters within the purview of Panchayats and Municipalities, enabling grassroots democratic governance and social auditing of welfare schemes.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary rationale behind subsuming multiple standalone educational schemes into the 'Samagra Shiksha' integrated framework?
opts: To reduce total budgetary allocation to the education sector by merging redundant ministries
To adopt a holistic, continuum-based approach from pre-school to senior secondary education, avoiding administrative fragmentation and optimizing resource utilization
To transfer the entire financial burden of schooling from the Central government to foreign multilateral institutions
To completely eliminate the role of state governments in designing school curricula and teacher recruitment
practiceQuestions.sol: Samagra Shiksha treats school education as a single continuum from pre-school to class 12. The idea is to harmonize disparate schemes (SSA, RMSA, Teacher Education) to ensure unified administrative oversight, flexible fund allocation, and holistic learning outcomes.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the PM POSHAN Scheme (formerly Mid-Day Meal Scheme) leverage the welfare state mechanism to address multi-dimensional developmental challenges in India?
opts: It exclusively targets adult literacy by distributing food grains to parents who send their children to coaching centers.
It addresses classroom hunger, enhances school participation, mitigates micro-nutrient deficiencies, and fosters social equality through shared meals across caste lines.
It functions as a commercial food procurement program to replace the Food Corporation of India buffer stocks.
It provides direct conditional cash transfers to private school owners based on student attendance metrics.
practiceQuestions.sol: PM POSHAN serves multiple developmental vectors: educational (improving enrollment, retention, and attentiveness), nutritional (combating classroom hunger and malnourishment), and social (breaking caste barriers as children eat together).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the core governance challenge associated with Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act regarding private school quotas for disadvantaged groups?
opts: Private schools refusing to accept any students from rural areas regardless of income brackets
Reimbursement delays by state governments to private schools and instances of social exclusion or discrimination within classrooms
Mandatory closure of all government primary schools in favor of exclusive private schooling
Total prohibition of English-medium instruction in elite private institutions
practiceQuestions.sol: Implementation bottlenecks for Section 12(1)(c) often include delayed or insufficient government reimbursements to private schools, administrative friction, and qualitative challenges regarding peer integration and potential social discrimination within elite schools.

practiceQuestions.q: How do digital educational welfare initiatives like DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) transform educational governance in India?
opts: By completely replacing physical classrooms and human teachers with autonomous artificial intelligence avatars
By providing a unified national digital platform offering high-quality e-content, teacher training courses, and QR-coded textbooks accessible across states
By serving exclusively as an online job portal for administrative bureaucrats in the Ministry of Education
By levying high subscription fees on marginalized students to fund private ed-tech corporations
practiceQuestions.sol: DIKSHA acts as the 'One Nation, One Digital Platform' for school education in India. It empowers teachers and students with curriculum-linked e-content, professional development courses, and pedagogical resources aligned with national frameworks.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the classification of Education under the Concurrent List a unique cooperative federalism mechanism in India?
opts: It prevents the Central government from enacting any laws related to education without unanimous consent from all states.
It allows both Parliament and State Legislatures to legislate on education, ensuring national standards (via central schemes and NCERT) while accommodating regional contexts and linguistic diversity.
It strips states of all administrative powers, vesting total authority over schools in the Prime Minister's Office.
It mandates that all educational institutions must be funded entirely through international philanthropic grants.
practiceQuestions.sol: Placing education in the Concurrent List exemplifies cooperative federalism by enabling national coordination, quality benchmarks, and centrally sponsored funding frameworks (like Samagra Shiksha) while respecting states' primary implementation role and cultural context.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of PM SHRI (Schools for Rising India) Scheme?
opts: To privatize all government-run schools in metropolitan cities
To upgrade selected existing government schools to showcase exemplary implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and serve as mentor schools
To provide free foreign education scholarships exclusively to civil service aspirants
To establish elite boarding schools in tribal districts managed entirely by multinational corporations
practiceQuestions.sol: PM SHRI is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at upgrading more than 14,500 existing government schools across India to reflect the vision of NEP 2020, featuring green school infrastructure, modern pedagogy, and holistic mentoring.

practiceQuestions.q: How do targeted educational scholarship schemes (like Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships for SC, ST, OBC, and Minorities) address structural inequities in Indian society?
opts: By offering unconditional cash payouts to all citizens regardless of their economic or social standing
By offsetting the opportunity costs of education and direct financial barriers faced by marginalized households, thereby preventing early dropouts and enabling upward social mobility
By funding luxury lifestyles for university students in metropolitan campuses
By replacing formal classroom instruction with mandatory vocational internships from primary school onwards
practiceQuestions.sol: Scholarship schemes act as affirmative action financial instruments that alleviate the direct and indirect costs of education for historically disadvantaged communities, bridging the dropout gap at critical transition stages (primary to secondary to higher education).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) in the governance of higher educational welfare and quality enhancement?
opts: It distributes government grants arbitrarily without evaluating institutional performance metrics
It establishes a transparent, objective methodology based on parameters like teaching, learning, research, and outreach to rank institutions, fostering healthy competitive excellence
It dictates the exact syllabus that every university must teach in humanities and sciences
It operates as a private auditing firm responsible for auditing foreign university campuses in India
practiceQuestions.sol: NIRF, launched by the Ministry of Education, provides a competitive ranking mechanism for higher educational institutions across India based on five broad parameters: Teaching, Learning & Resources, Research & Professional Practice, Graduation Outcomes, Outreach & Inclusivity, and Perception.

practiceQuestions.q: How do Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) address gender disparities in educational welfare within remote and backward regions?
opts: By providing residential upper-primary and secondary schools specifically for girls from SC, ST, OBC, and minority communities in educationally backward blocks
By offering evening coaching classes exclusively for male dropouts in urban slums
By operating as elite sports academies funded by corporate CSR sponsorships
By functioning as vocational training centers exclusively for adult women entrepreneurs
practiceQuestions.sol: KGBV is a scheme launched to set up residential schools at the upper primary level for girls belonging predominantly to the disadvantaged groups (SC, ST, OBC, and Minority) in Educationally Backward Blocks (EBBs), ensuring access and retention.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009:
1. It applies to all schools across India, including unaided private schools and minority-run institutions.
2. It prohibits the screening procedure for admission of children and mandates that no child shall be held back or expelled in any class until completion of elementary education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 30(1) minority-run institutions (aided or unaided) are exempt from the provisions of the RTE Act as per Supreme Court rulings (Pramati Educational Trust case). Statement 2 is partially incorrect because subsequent amendments to the RTE Act (2019) permitted schools to hold regular examinations in classes 5 and 8, and if a child fails, provision is made for re-examination.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Samagra Shiksha Scheme:
1. It is a centrally sponsored scheme that subsumes Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), and Teacher Education (TE).
2. Its financial funding pattern between the Centre and States is uniform at 50:50 for all states and Union Territories without legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the funding pattern is 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States, 100% for UTs without legislature, and 60:40 for other States and UTs with legislature, not a uniform 50:50.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the PM POSHAN Scheme:
1. It covers children studying in classes I to VIII in government, aided, and local body schools.
2. The nutritional norms under the scheme mandate a minimum of 450 calories and 12 grams of protein per child per day for primary stage students.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. PM POSHAN (formerly Mid-Day Meal Scheme) covers children in classes I-VIII (primary and upper primary). The specified nutritional norm for primary stage (I-V) is 450 calories and 12 grams of protein, and for upper primary (VI-VIII) is 700 calories and 20 grams of protein.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 recommendations on school education:
1. It replaces the 10+2 school structure with a new 5+3+3+4 curricular structure corresponding to ages 3-8, 8-11, 11-14, and 14-18 years.
2. It mandates mother tongue or local language as the medium of instruction compulsorily up to Grade 8 wherever possible.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (5+3+3+4 structure covering ages 3-18). Statement 2 is incorrect because NEP 2020 recommends medium of instruction in mother tongue/local language 'preferably' up to Grade 5, and wherever possible up to Grade 8, but it is not strictly mandated up to Grade 8.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the NIPUN Bharat Mission:
1. It is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
2. Its primary objective is to achieve universal acquisition of foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) by the end of Grade 3.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because NIPUN Bharat is launched by the Department of School Education and Literacy under the Ministry of Education, not the Ministry of Women and Child Development. Statement 2 is correct (targeting FLN by Grade 3).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA):
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme providing strategic funding to state higher educational institutions.
2. Central funding to states under RUSA is contingent upon academic, administrative, and financial reforms in state universities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. RUSA aims to improve the quality of state universities and colleges through targeted funding, which is strictly tied to governance reforms, institutional accreditation (NAAC), and financial accountability.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Constitutional provisions for education in India:
1. Article 21A was inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
2. Article 350A directs every state to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are factually correct. Article 21A establishes the fundamental right to elementary education, while Article 350A (added by the 7th Amendment Act, 1956) mandates states to provide mother tongue instruction facilities to linguistic minorities.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding PM SHRI Schools:
1. It is a centrally sponsored scheme to develop more than 14,500 schools as exemplar schools showcasing all components of the National Education Policy 2020.
2. Selection of schools under PM SHRI is done through a challenge mode where schools compete to fulfill specific infrastructure and governance benchmarks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. PM SHRI schools act as role models in their respective regions, embodying NEP 2020 tenets, and are selected through a rigorous competitive challenge mode based on preset quality parameters.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mid-Day Meal Scheme / PM POSHAN:
1. The Supreme Court of India in PUCL v. Union of India (2001) directed all state governments to implement the mid-day meal scheme in all government and government-aided primary schools.
2. The food security allowance must be provided by the state government if the mid-day meal cannot be provided to school children on any school day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Supreme Court landmark order in the PUCL Right to Food case institutionalized mid-day meals. Additionally, under the National Food Security Act (NFSA) 2013, if meals are not provided, the state must pay a food security allowance.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding educational governance institutions in India:
1. The University Grants Commission (UGC) is a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament in 1956 for the coordination, determination, and maintenance of standards in university education.
2. The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) is a constitutional body created under Article 282 to advise central and state governments on school education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because NCERT is not a constitutional body; it is an autonomous literary, scientific, and charitable society registered under the Societies Registration Act (Act XXI of 1860).
